critical_steps: The repeated unit vector is not Bessel.
The indefinite invertible controller C makes every controlled Gram entry zero.
The published proof incorrectly discards coefficients of a vector orthogonal to U-star C f_k rather than to f_k.
When U-star C is positive invertible, the controlled Gram is the ordinary Gram of (U-star C)^(1/2) f_k.
Bounded ordinary Gram matrices are equivalent to Bessel sequences.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional isotropic-vector counterexample and reduction to an ordinary Gram matrix under a positive controller product.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest possible nonpositive coercive controller condition is classified.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects Lemma 2.6 and does not reassess every downstream theorem in the paper.
Positivity and invertibility of U-star C give an exact repaired equivalence, but are not claimed to be the weakest possible controller hypothesis in every setting.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: An indefinite controller can hide a non-Bessel sequence from the controlled Gram matrix
